title: Signals data backfill migrations: non-atomic, batched, self-contained, acknowledged in txt file
answers: How do I write a batched backfill migration in signals?
Why is my non-atomic migration failing the migration check?
Should a backfill migration reuse live model parsing code?
body:
Pattern from `products/signals/backend/migrations/0154_backfill_report_actionability.py`:
- `atomic = False`, id-ordered batches (cursor `id__gt`), only selecting rows still unfilled so it is resumable; `RunPython(..., RunPython.noop, elidable=True)`.
- Every non-atomic migration needs an entry plus explanatory comment in `posthog/management/migration_analysis/atomic_false_acknowledged_migrations.txt` (format `signals.0154_...`).
- Update `products/signals/backend/migrations/max_migration.txt` with the new migration name.
- Parse in Python inside the migration using historical models, not the live parser (`report_actionability_repair`): an applied migration must not change when live code changes. Skip malformed rows instead of failing the deploy (no SQL `IS JSON` on PG15).
- Use `update()`, not `save()`, so `updated_at` (used for inbox sorting) is not bumped; repeat the NULL conditions in the UPDATE to avoid overwriting a concurrent receiver write.
- Unknown actionability strings are cached as-is (matching receivers), only overlong values are dropped.
applies: Data migrations in products/signals; non-atomic migrations repo-wide
